Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Opinion Global hegemons and the discussion for peace: Negative peace, positive peace or economic peace? Source : Victor Doke 24 November 2026 6:27pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The three world leaders, President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on November 19, 2026, held a maiden edition of a tripartite engagement ostensibly to talk about peace. With the leaders declaring peace, will it be just a rhetoric or reality? Will these world leaders see to it that the negative peace concept is realized? Or will they empower international organizations such as the United Nations to facilitate positive peace in the global spectrum, where these three leaders play crucial roles in ensuring that the objective of negative peace is met?
The United States of America, Russia, and China are all vetoes in the in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and known largest nuclear powers. What this means is that every decision taken outside of the UNSC needs to have cooperation among the individual states. With the meeting described as historic, the question is, what are the objective/s of these three leaders regarding what has been highlighted by the international media as a declaration for peace? The central conversation at the meeting was to commit to denuclearization and curb the consequences regarding nuclear proliferation. Will these leaders trust each other to the extent of limiting nuclear stockpiles? Or this meeting is one of those just for the optics?
Russia is currently at war with Ukraine, USA is leading ‘military operations’ against Iran but China is not actively engaged in any armed conflict, but tensions remain in the South China Sea and around Taiwan. This is because China’s military drills and deployments, along with territorial disputes with India, Japan and Bhutan, make the situation in that region uncertain. With concrete actions taken by Russia and the USA regarding their role in the armed conflict in Ukraine and Iran, respectively, the lens is on China regarding what will happen next. Will China also exhibit tendencies as Russia and the USA, or will it really commit to peace as the meeting makes us to believe?
Scholars, practitioners, and experts in the peace, security, and international relations field have questioned whether the actions of Russia, the USA, and China could be stopped. The United Nations (UN) has been accused of not enforcing its mandate to ensure international peace and security. This is due to the fact that the UN could not stop the actions of these states. If the UN could not stop the states from their current actions in the Middle East, Ukraine, and elsewhere, would they in the future when any states unilaterally violate international law? The uncertainty is also related to the fact that the President of the USA as the Chairman of the Board of Peace, together with Mr. Putin and Mr. Xi did not mention the specific target for which peace needs to be achieved.
These three global powers dominate the political and security landscape in their respective regions. The question arises if their actions amount to self-interest regarding how these leaders exhibit tendencies of power play and exert coercion in security. The ideal decision on the peace declaration would be to announce a vivid conviction regarding specificity in the commitment to peace and in the respective armed conflicts they are engaged in.
The UN seem to be having a challenge regarding what to do, sanctions are not forthcoming. These leaders seem to take decisions at any given time without recourse to the effects on the global stage. Accusations are that, so far as these actions taken satisfies their national interest and satisfaction then it should be implemented. Regional organizations such as the European Union (EU), North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) are also watching events unfold whilst their opinions and suggestions are not considered. World peace seems to be at a crossroads at this moment, and the argument has been established that these three leaders have the authority to address the insecurities and resolve the conflicts for lasting peace to prevail.
We are economically interconnected. The Russia-Ukraine conflict gave us a glimpse of how worst we are ill-prepared for any global crises as a continent. As a result of the on-going conflict in the Middle East, fuel prices skyrocketed and the effects were felt at the pumps. When the pumps record high prices, it has rippling effects on every facet of the economy and that has been the story of most states in the Global South. The current Middle East armed conflict is protracting; we could continue to experience more economic and financial shocks in the micro and macro sectors of the economy. This can be addressed with the assistance of regional and sub-regional organizations such as the African Union (AU), the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), and Regional Economic Communities (RECs), respectively, implementing economic policies that will enable states to withstand any shock.
The power play is real, and unfortunately the rest of the world is at the receiving end of that power play and self-interest. In the name of sovereignty, some powerful states get away with wrongdoing, violate international laws and treaties. The values and norms on which international organizations such as the UN were established seem to be eroding because of the anarchy in the global governance spectrum. We need to be intentional and commit to peace. Peace is not just mere rhetoric but action. The absence of war is good, but if the structural variables that enable insecurity persist, we will end up with armed conflicts and not the absence of it.
